items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: Anyhow I took an audition with a man called — let me see if I remember his name — Steinberg.

ctx.x: I see. Well you had an opportunity to work with the Buffalo Philharmonic?

No I never played but I was offered the position with them. I never played. But I took an audition, and that sounds very familiar. That rhymes — position and audition. Anyhow I took an audition with a man called — let me see if I remember his name — Steinberg. He was a conductor of the Buffalo Symphony Orchestra. I’m pretty sure that was his name, [William] Steinberg. And they offered me the job, like $75, but we had to move to Buffalo. And my wife, who was my manager and agent, she said let’s stay in New York.…
Did you work — I’m sorry, you were in the service, right? In the Army?
